summary_en: Notification on the occurrence of the obligatory memorial of the Immaculate Heart of the Blessed Virgin Mary (raised to obligatory memorial in the General Roman Calendar by the decree of 1 January 1996, Prot. 2376/95/L) with another obligatory memorial on the same day: in such a year both memorials are to be kept as optional memorials, following the Instruction Calendaria particularia n. 23c; the first such occurrence falls in 2003.
excerpt: In casu quo praedicta memoria, cuius dies celebrationis mobilis est ac dependens a die celebrationis Paschatis, eodem die occurrat una cum altera memoria obligatoria, illo anno hae duae memoriae tamquam ad libitum retineri debent, iuxta indicationes quae in Instructione Calendaria particularia diei 24 iunii 1970 relate ad calendaria particularia (n. 23c) inveniuntur.

summary_en: Notification «De titulo ecclesiae»: general norms on the title of a church and on patrons; a church's title must be the Trinity, the Lord, the Holy Spirit, the Blessed Virgin, the holy angels or a Saint or Blessed inscribed in the Roman Martyrology (n. 2); only one title unless the Saints are inscribed together in the proper calendar (n. 3); a Blessed not yet inscribed in the legitimate diocesan calendar cannot be chosen as title without an indult (n. 4); a patron must be a created person, never the Trinity or a divine Person (n. 8); the election of a patron has liturgical effect only when confirmed by decree of this Congregation (n. 9); the patron of a place is distinct from a church's title (n. 10). Recorded as a general norm touching titular and patronal celebrations; review whether it belongs in the register.
excerpt: 9. Patronus eligendus est a clero et a fidelibus, quae electio approbanda est a competenti auctoritate ecclesiastica. Ut effectum liturgicum habeantur, electio et approbatio indigent confirmatione Congregationis de Culto Divino et Disciplina Sacramentorum, quae decreto eiusdem Dicasterii conceditur.

summary_en: Decree on the feast of the Blessed Virgin Mary of Guadalupe: following the Apostolic Exhortation Ecclesia in America (22 January 1999), the celebration of Our Lady of Guadalupe is to be inscribed on 12 December in the calendars of every nation and territory of America with the grade of feast, to be celebrated yearly in every diocese of the continent, without prejudice to concessions of the grade of solemnity already granted to particular circumscriptions and churches; Spanish texts annexed as textus typici.
excerpt: Istud igitur Dicasterium hoc festum declarat in calendariis cuiusque nationis vel territorii Americae ad diem 12 decembris inscribendum, ut in singulis Continentis dioecesibus eo die quotannis celebretur, salvis semper concessionibus gradus sollemnitatis ab Apostolica Sede in favorem quarundam circumscriptionum et ecclesiarum decreto vel norma iam peractis.

summary_en: Apostolic Letter motu proprio «Spes aedificandi» (John Paul II, 1 October 1999): St Bridget of Sweden, St Catherine of Siena and St Teresa Benedicta of the Cross (Edith Stein) are proclaimed co-patronesses of the whole of Europe, with the liturgical honours and privileges that belong by law to principal patrons of places; a French version follows on pp. 413-425.
excerpt: Omnibus itaque mature ponderatis rationibus, Nostra utentes Apostolica potestate, creamus ac caelestes ante Deum universae Europae compatronas pronuntiamus sanctam Birgittam de Suetia, sanctam Catharinam Senensem, sanctam Teresiam Benedictam a Cruce, tributis nimirum honoribus simul cunctis et privilegiis liturgicis quae principalibus locorum conveniunt iure patronis.

summary_en: Notification «De cultu Beatorum»: general norms on the liturgical cult of Blesseds and their place in particular calendars: a Blessed's celebration is assigned to the dies natalis, or to the nearest free day when impeded (n. 5); in the particular calendar of a diocese, religious family or wider territory it is an optional memorial, an obligatory memorial in the church where the relics are kept, and the grade of feast is generally reserved to the founder in his institute's calendar (n. 6); only Blesseds of particular significance are to be inscribed in the whole diocese or institute (n. 7); a Blessed already inscribed in the particular calendar may be chosen as titular of a church without indult and is then celebrated there as a feast (n. 9); a Blessed may be chosen as patron of a place or association with confirmation of the Holy See (n. 10); Blesseds without a formal decree may be kept in a particular calendar marked with an asterisk (n. 14).
excerpt: 6. Celebratio cuiuslibet Beati in Calendario particulari dioecesis vel familiae religiosae vel in amplioris territorii legitime inscripti gradu memoriae ad libitum fit et gradu memoriae obligatoriae in ecclesia, in qua exuviae eius asservantur; gradus vero festi plerumque reservatur in Calendario Instituti religiosi Beato, qui illius Instituti fundator fuit.

summary_en: Circular letter to the presidents of the episcopal conferences of Europe: from the year 2000 the celebrations of St Bridget, religious (23 July), St Catherine of Siena, virgin and doctor of the Church (29 April) and St Teresa Benedicta of the Cross, virgin and martyr (9 August) are to be kept every year with the grade of feast in all calendars and Ordines of the dioceses of Europe; where by particular law they are already celebrated on another day or as solemnities, that day and grade are retained; Latin Mass and Office texts are annexed (pp. 449-453).
excerpt: 1. A vertente anno 2000 celebrationes – S. Birgittae, religiosae, die 23 iulii; – S. Catharinae Senensis, virginis et Ecclesiae Doctoris, die 29 aprilis; – S. Benedictae a Cruce, virginis et martyris, die 9 augusti quotannis gradu Festi peragendae erunt.
